correctness.rationale: The published conditional sign-flip property reduces the complete-null rule exactly to iid fair signs. Algebra turns the reciprocal Knockoff+ prefix criterion into first hitting of level r by a +1/-r walk. Strong Markov factorization gives F(z)^r, Lagrange inversion gives the exact coefficients, and exact-rational dynamic programming plus exhaustive short-string checks replay the identities.

originality.rationale: The inspected knockoff sources establish sign symmetry, FDR control, +1 necessity, and stopping-time/e-value interpretations, but none of the inspected material states the complete-null reciprocal-level finite Fuss-Catalan law or the limiting root formula. Targeted semantic searches also returned no equivalent record. Residual older ballot/competition literature risk is retained.
residual_risks: The same all-null specialization may appear in older target-decoy, ballot-theorem, or sequential-testing literature under different notation.

Because the first-passage coefficients are classical, novelty attaches to the exact Knockoff+ identification and calibration consequence, not to Lagrange inversion or generalized Catalan numbers themselves.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies an exact finite-sample and asymptotic calibration baseline for a widely used FDR procedure and quantifies severe complete-null conservatism at q=0.1. It distinguishes the nominal worst-case guarantee from attained all-null error and is useful for implementation checks and for assessing approximate/dependent variants.
